task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 25, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper news update about a film studio's proposed local-crew agreement in Thornhaven and the difference between announced commitments and funded production work.

facts.text: Thornhaven Screenworks published a proposed local-hiring agreement on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, alongside an application for a county production grant.
The company seeks $600,000 toward converting two warehouse bays into sound stages; the grant board will consider applications in October.
No award has been made, and the company has not begun the conversion.
The proposal sets aside 12 paid trainee placements if the stages open and a first production contract is signed.
Each placement would last 16 weeks, with 30 scheduled paid hours a week at a gross hourly rate of $18; individual deductions are not supplied.
The placements would cover lighting, set construction and production administration, rather than acting roles.
Applicants would need to live in the county when applying, but the proposal sets no length-of-residence requirement.
The company has letters of interest from two producers, neither of which is a binding production contract.
The application estimates a peak production crew of 70 people during a full shoot, including the 12 trainees if all placements are filled; it is not a count of permanent year-round jobs.
Studio founder Iven Tal said production schedules may leave periods between shoots when no freelance crew are engaged.
Tal said, "A stage can be a permanent building while the work inside it comes in blocks."
Set carpenter Rena Doss currently travels out of the county for most jobs and would welcome shorter trips.
Doss said trainees also need safe storage for their tools and a way to travel home after late calls.
Doss said, "Training gets somebody onto the first call sheet. The next call is the harder promise."
The proposal includes a county-college training partner but no guaranteed job after a placement ends.
The college has agreed to help design instruction; its governing board has not approved a new degree program.
The warehouse landlord has signed a conditional lease that takes effect if project financing closes by February 2027.
The county grant program scores applications on paid training, local purchasing and evidence of financing, not solely on headline job estimates.
One warehouse bay previously held theatrical scenery and the other remains occupied by a furniture wholesaler until December.
The public application does not disclose the founders' full private financing commitments or establish a final stage-opening date.
